answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may influence high-stakes votes. The protocol caps each identity’s voting weight and lets established peers slash the bond when a newcomer’s claims fail repeated, independently checked tasks. A cedar garden may welcome many honest agents, but an attacker must tie up real capital in every fake identity and risk losing it, making a mass Sybil swarm costly rather than free. The ledge is the delay before influence begins.
